Triggers Automated database behaviors prevent bad states from leaking into the system and handle real-time calculation tasks. 10.1 Trigger Name: trg_sync_account_delinquency Event: AFTER UPDATE on billing_accounts Purpose: Tracks status adjustments to trigger real-time communications to customers,

_sync_account_delinquency Event: AFTER UPDATE on billing_accounts Purpose: Tracks status adjustments to trigger real-time communications to customers, preventing customer churn and keeping user accounts active. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_evaluate_delinquency() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$ BEGIN IF NEW.current_balance > 100.00 AND NEW.account_status = 'ACTIVE' THEN -- Set account status to delinquent UPDATE billing_accounts SET account_status = 'DELINQUENT', updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE account_id = NEW.account_id; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql; CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_account_delinquency AFTER UPDATE OF current_balance ON billing_accounts FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION fn_evaluate_delinquency(); 11. Non-prime fields map directly to their full primary structures. Third Normal Form (3NF): Enforced. No transitive dependencies are present. Field updates remain isolated, preventing updates from cascading across unrelated tables. Deliberate Denormalization Strategy: The table transactions_log deviates from third normal form by storing a JSONB object: gateway_response_payload . Storing this unstructured data in JSONB prevents database locking delays and avoids complex child tables, ensuring fast transaction logging during peak checkout activity. 14. on Strategy This section outlines the steps to safely migrate production traffic from our legacy system to the modernized Project Nexus infrastructure with minimal downtime. 18.1 Schema Versioning & Deployments All database structure changes are written in SQL and managed using Liquibase. Every change is tracked as a version-controlled migration script, and these scripts are applied automatically during deployment pipeline updates. 18.2 Zero-Downtime Blue-Green Cutover Pattern To protect our systems during deployment, we use a Blue-Green deployment pattern to cut over active web and mobile traffic: Database Replication: We set up a new production database instance (Green) running the updated Project Nexus schema, and replicate data from the active production database (Blue) in real time

duction database instance (Green) running the updated Project Nexus schema, and replicate data from the active production database (Blue) in real time using AWS Database Migration Service (DMS). Verification Phase: We run validation queries on the Green instance to ensure all data is consistent and accurate. Traffic Redirection: Once validated, we update route controls to safely point consumer-facing applications to the Green instance. Fallback Option: We keep the old Blue database online and synchronized for 48 hours, allowing us to roll back immediately if any unexpected issues occur.
